procedural_matters: The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
Hearing No. 2 was heard together with hearing No. 3 in accordance with RRS 63.(2)(b) since both hearings arose from very closely connected incidents.
FRA 2948 was represented by Alexis Hauzy.
HUN 3352 was represented by Samuel Andreas Juhasz
RC was represented by Fabian Bach
Bence Szalontai (coach of HUN 3352) attended the hearing as an observer
HUN presented video evidence during the hearing.
Julia (member of the PC) gave evidence as a witness.
facts: The incident occurred in race Q2, close to mark 1, leg 3.
A ferry motored towards course area Alpha, entered the course area and went through the fleet from the windward side of the course area.
The race committee has no control over the movements of the ferry.
The ferry was driving on its commerical ferry corridor from Schilksee to Kiel City.
FRA 2948 was sailing on port tack on a close-hauled course aiming to the stern of the ferry.
When FRA 2948 passed the ferry astern, she capsized.
HUN 3352 on starboard tack, close-hauled on the layline was approaching FRA 2948.
When HUN 3352 was at mast of the capsized boat, she luffed and tacked into the propeller wash of the ferry.
Both boats lost positions as a result of the ferry passing through the course area.
The RC was aware of the situation that the ferry entered the course and decided to continue with the race.
There was neither damage nor injury.
conclusions: There was neither an improper action nor omission by the RC, PC, TC or OA and therefore the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(1) are not met.
Since the ferry did not cause damage or injury, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(3) are not met.
